message.content:
It’s hard to pick just one “best” film from 2020 because tastes vary so much, but here are a few titles that received widespread acclaim and are often cited as standout releases of that year:

| Film | Director | Why it stood out |
|------|----------|------------------|
| **Parasite** (re‑release) | Bong Joon‑ho | Though released in 2019, it dominated 2020 awards circuits and won Best Picture at the Oscars. |
| **Soul** | Pete Docter & Kemp Powers | Pixar’s Oscar‑winning animated feature about life’s purpose and jazz music. |
| **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | A high‑concept action thriller that pushed the limits of time‑travel storytelling. |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | A courtroom drama that captured the political climate of the late 1960s with sharp dialogue. |
| **Nomadland** | Chloé Zhao | A quiet, contemplative look at modern American nomads that earned Zhao an Oscar for Best Director. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best” according to critics, many lists rank **Parasite** (for its global impact and critical reception) or **Nomadland** (for its artistic depth and award success). If you prefer genre films, **Tenet** and **Soul** were the most talked‑about releases. Ultimately, the “best” will depend on your personal taste—whether you favor narrative depth, technical innovation, or emotional resonance.
